answer: Coordinated Action Surcharge. Each agent action carries a fee that scales with how many other agents act in the same tick on the same target; fees are pooled and rebated to agents whose behavior stays uncorrelated. An attacker running many identities must either pay escalating surcharges for synchronized action or spread activity thinly, weakening impact. Like a sable slipping through a crowded garden, duplicates cannot hide in the herd, and each fake identity adds a recurring dune of predictable cost.
